blocos.titulo: How to recognise the letters on the street
blocos.explicacao: How to recognise the letters on the street. Here is a mental exercise that changes everything. Imagine you are in Russia and you see a sign. You look at the sign and try to recognise the letters. Let's practise with real signs. Sign 1: РЕСТОРАН Р = R Е = YE С = S Т = T О = O Р = R А = A Н = N Result: RESTORAN = Restaurant. Sign 2: МЕТРО М = M Е = YE Т = T Р = R О = O Result: METRO = Metro. Sign 3: АПТЕКА А = A П = P Т = T Е = YE К = K А = A Result: APTEKA = Pharmacy. Sign 4: БАНК Б = B А = A Н = N К = K Result: BANK = Bank. Sign 5: ОТЕЛЬ О = O Т = T Е = YE Л = L Ь = soft sign Result: OTEL = Hotel. Sign 6: ТЕАТР Т = T Е = YE А = A Т = T Р = R Result: TEATR = Theatre. Notice: you have just read six Russian signs. Without memorising a complicated alphabet. Without suffering. That is what the Russian alphabet does. It is much friendlier than it looks.

blocos.titulo: Hard vowels and soft vowels: the key to the consonants
blocos.explicacao: Hard vowels and soft vowels: the key to the consonants. Here is a concept you need to understand from the start. It will appear in every lesson that follows. Russian vowels come in two families: HARD vowels (5): SOFT vowels (5): Notice: А ↔ Я (a ↔ ya) О ↔ Ё (o ↔ yo) У ↔ Ю (oo ↔ yoo) Э ↔ Е (e ↔ ye) Ы ↔ И (throaty ee ↔ ee) Each hard vowel has a matching soft vowel. This is fundamental because: when a consonant comes before a soft vowel, it is pronounced "softened" (palatalised). When it comes before a hard vowel, it is "hard". Examples: но (noh) → hard "n" нё (nyo) → softened "n" ну (noo) → hard "n" ню (nyoo) → softened "n" For now, you do not need to worry about this. But know that: the soft vowels (Я, Ё, Ю, Е, И) are the "secret" to understanding Russian consonants. Whenever you see one of these letters after a consonant, the consonant is "soft". We will see this in practice in the next section.

blocos.titulo: Voiceless and voiced consonants; cursive handwriting
blocos.explicacao: Voiceless and voiced consonants. In Russian, consonants fall into two groups, forming pairs: How it works: Voiceless consonants are pronounced without vibration of the vocal cords (like "p", "f", "k", "t", "s", "sh"). Voiced consonants are pronounced with vibration of the vocal cords (like "b", "v", "g", "d", "z", "zh"). The rule: when a voiced consonant is at the end of a word, it is pronounced as the matching voiceless one. Examples: This is why "друг" sounds like "drook". The letter Г at the end of the word becomes К. How to write in Russian cursive. An important detail: Russians write in cursive very often. You will see handwritten texts with letters different from the printed ones. Here is a small table of the main differences: For now, focus on the printed letters. When you come across handwritten Russian texts, you will learn cursive little by little.

linhas.pt: — My name is Ivan. Nice to meet you!

blocos.ru: Преподаватель входит в класс и говорит: «Здравствуйте! Меня зовут Иван Петрович. А как вас зовут?» Студентка отвечает: «Меня зовут Лена. Очень приятно!» Преподаватель говорит: «Мне тоже очень приятно, Лена!»
blocos.pt: The teacher comes into the room and says: «Hello! My name is Ivan Petrovich. And what is your name?» The student answers: «My name is Lena. Nice to meet you!» The teacher says: «Nice to meet you too, Lena!»

blocos.enunciado: Repeat the dialogue. Then introduce yourself aloud: «Привет! Меня зовут… Очень приятно!»
